subject: lenPeerRecv
why: two len(ch) reads around a pure registry-free recursion while a child's RECEIVE drains a pre-filled cap-2 buffer: the channel-length apply is an L1 scheduling point (BUG-123), so the receive lands before the first read (11), between the two (21) or after both (22); certified set {11, 21, 22} (members=3); gc exhibits all three (300 plain: 22 ×293, 21 ×7; 300 -race: 21 ×225, 22 ×68, 11 ×7); width 4 >= the two-goroutine scheduler bound and the exit window

subject: lenBesideClose
why: closing never changes the buffer count (spec#Close): both reads see 1 on every schedule, the closed channel still delivers its element then the zero value with ok=false — 11111 on every schedule

subject: capBesideSend
why: a channel's capacity never changes, so cap(ch) observes no peer and opens no scheduling point (the sched-boundary design's argument) — 33 on every schedule

subject: lenUnbufferedParkedSender
why: an unbuffered channel has no buffer, so len is 0 beside a parked sender on every schedule (gc's chanlen reads qcount); the value arrives by pairing — 700 on every schedule

subject: printlnMultiOperandAtomic
why:
one println with three operands is one statement under gc's printlock and one print apply on the machine, so a peer's println lands before or after the whole line, never between its operands: certified set {"a b c
x y z
", "x y z
a b c
"} (members=2); gc exhibits both (300 plain 298/2, 300 -race 288/12)

subject: deferredPrintDrain
why: a print in a deferred call at the child's normal drain is a scheduling point like any print: main's A lands before B, between B and D, or after D; certified set {ABD, BAD, BDA} (members=3)

subject: deferredPrintUnwinding
why: a print in a deferred call during the child's panic UNWINDING (post-raise, recovered) is a scheduling point: main's A lands before B, between B and R, or after R; certified set {ABR, BAR, BRA} (members=3)

subject: printInsideCallee
why: a call is no scheduling point but the print inside the callee is: certified set {AB, BA} (members=2)
